checks.label: Default Encryption Password Check
checks.description: Safe ONLY when '0'. '1' means encryption uses default password, which is insecure. Strict anchoring avoids matching numbers inside longer strings.
checks.remediation: Set a strong user-chosen encryption password via Settings > Security. Avoid leaving the default password in place.

checks.label: Encryption Completion Status
checks.description: Full Disk Encryption is complete only if output is exactly '1'. A strict equality match ensures no accidental pattern hits.
checks.remediation: If encryption is incomplete, reboot and allow it to finish. If it fails, re-initiate encryption from recovery mode.

checks.label: Data Partition Encryption Check
checks.command: T=$(getprop ro.crypto.type 2>/dev/null); S=$(getprop ro.crypto.state 2>/dev/null); M=$(mount 2>/dev/null | grep ' /data ' | grep -oE '^[^ ]+'); echo "state=${S:-unset} type=${T:-unset} dev=${M:-unknown}"
checks.description: Confirms /data is encrypted, reading ro.crypto.state and ro.crypto.type rather than looking for a dm- device in the mount table. The earlier version required the /data mount source to match 'dm-', which is only true for full-disk or metadata encryption. File-based encryption, the default since Android 10, encrypts per file and mounts the raw partition directly, so on a correctly encrypted FBE device the mount source is something like /dev/block/mmcblk0p78 and the check reported a critical finding on a device whose ro.crypto.state was encrypted. Verified on a Samsung SM-M025F with type=file and state=encrypted.
checks.remediation: Enable device encryption so /data is mounted via dm-crypt. Back up data first, then encrypt from Settings or recovery.

checks.label: FBE FUSE Layer Status
checks.description: File-Based Encryption is active only if output is exactly 'true'. Anchors prevent accidental matches of longer boolean strings.
checks.remediation: Enable file-based encryption (FBE) in device settings or reflash with an FBE-enabled firmware image.

checks.label: Service-Based Encryption Check
checks.description: Encryption is typically active when the response contains '00000001'. Because binder output is structured, this specific pattern is reliable with minimal false-positive risk.
checks.remediation: Enable device encryption via Settings > Security. If the mount service reports inactive, reboot and retry.

checks.label: SD Card Encryption
checks.description: Safe ONLY when output is exactly '1'. Strict match prevents accidental detection from logs or metadata containing '1'.
checks.remediation: Encrypt the SD card via Settings > Security > Encrypt SD card. Remove sensitive data from unencrypted cards.

checks.label: SD Card Mount Check
checks.description: Safe if SD card is mounted via dm-crypt or FUSE. Pattern is strict enough to avoid accidental substring matches on unrelated mount entries.
checks.remediation: Encrypt the SD card so it mounts through dm-crypt or FUSE. Reformat and re-encrypt if mounted as plain storage.

checks.label: Crypto FS State
checks.description: Filesystem decryption state
checks.remediation: If decryption is stalled, reboot the device. Ensure a valid encryption password is set to allow proper unlock.

checks.label: StrongBox Support
checks.description: StrongBox secure element support
checks.remediation: Use a device with StrongBox support for highest key protection. Migrate critical keys to hardware-backed storage.

checks.label: Hardcoded Passwords in Config
checks.description: Config files containing password-related keywords (keyword detection - verify manually whether actual credentials are present)
checks.remediation: Remove hardcoded passwords from config files. Use a secrets manager or environment variables instead.

checks.label: API Keys in Files
checks.description: Files containing API key-related keywords (keyword detection - verify manually whether actual secrets are present)
checks.remediation: Remove API keys from files. Store them in Android Keystore or a secure secrets management solution.

checks.label: Private Keys Exposed
checks.command: find /system /vendor /data /sdcard -type f \( -name '*.pem' -o -name '*.key' \) | head -40 | while read f; do grep -lqE 'BEGIN (RSA |EC |DSA |OPENSSH |ENCRYPTED )?PRIVATE KEY' "$f" 2>/dev/null && echo "$f"; done | head -10; find /system /vendor /data /sdcard -type f \( -name '*.p12' -o -name '*.pfx' \) 2>/dev/null | head -10
checks.description: Files containing actual private-key material (PEM private-key headers, or .p12/.pfx keystores). Public .pem certificates shipped in the system image are NOT flagged - the check greps file contents for a PRIVATE KEY header rather than matching on the .pem name, which previously false-flagged public CA certs.
checks.remediation: Delete unnecessary private key files. Move required keys to hardware-backed storage with strict permissions.

checks.label: SSH Keys on Device
checks.description: SSH keys found - review if needed
checks.remediation: Remove SSH keys that are not required. Restrict file permissions to owner-only (chmod 600) for any that remain.

checks.command: find /system /vendor -type f \( -name 'shadow' -o -name 'credentials*' \); find /system /vendor -type f -name 'passwd' | while read f; do grep -Eq ':\$[0-9a-z]+\$' "$f" 2>/dev/null && echo "$f"; done
checks.label: Default Credential Files
checks.description: Credential files with real secrets: a 'shadow' file, a 'credentials*' file, or a 'passwd' file that actually contains a hashed password ($1$/$5$/$6$). Android's standard /system/etc/passwd is an AID-to-name map with no hashes and is present on every device, so it is no longer flagged on its name alone (previous false positive).
checks.remediation: Remove default credential files from /system and /vendor. Use Android Keystore for credential management.

checks.label: Hardcoded URLs with Credentials
checks.description: URLs with embedded user:password@host credentials. The userinfo and host are restricted to URL-safe characters (no spaces, quotes or angle brackets) so the regex no longer spans across XML/doc text - the previous loose pattern false-matched 'https://developer.android.com/... @UserHandleAware' in framework config files.
checks.remediation: Replace embedded credentials in URLs with token-based auth or secure credential storage.

checks.label: Credential Strings in Local Databases
checks.command: find /data /sdcard -type f \( -name '*.db' -o -name '*.sqlite' -o -name '*.sqlite3' \) | head -40 | while IFS= read -r f; do grep -laiE 'password|passwd|api[_-]?key|client[_-]?secret|bearer |refresh[_-]?token' "$f" 2>/dev/null; done | head -10
checks.description: Searches the first 40 SQLite databases found under /data and /sdcard for credential-looking strings (password, api_key, client_secret, bearer, refresh_token) and lists the files that contain them. SQLite stores text unencrypted in the page data, so a credential written into a table is readable straight out of the file by anyone who can read it. The earlier version of this check carried the same label but only listed .db filenames and never inspected their contents, which duplicated the database inventory in privacy.json. Capped at 40 files scanned and 10 reported so the scan stays bounded on a device with a large /data.
checks.remediation: Inspect each listed database. Move credentials into the Android Keystore or EncryptedSharedPreferences instead of a plain SQLite table, and confirm the file is not world-readable.

checks.label: KeyMint HAL Present
checks.description: KeyMint HAL (Android 12+) provides stronger key attestation and hardware-backed cryptography than legacy Keymaster. Absence may indicate an older or less-secure keystore implementation.
checks.remediation: Update to Android 12+ firmware with KeyMint HAL support. Avoid relying on legacy Keymaster for key attestation.

checks.label: Kernel Entropy Pool Size
checks.description: /proc/sys/kernel/random/entropy_avail reports available entropy in bits. Modern kernels (5.18+) maintain a fixed 256 once seeded, older kernels report up to 4096. Values below about 256 at runtime indicate a starved CSPRNG, which weakens every TLS handshake and key generation. Embedded boards often boot with very low entropy.
checks.remediation: On embedded boards, enable a hardware RNG (TRNG, virtio-rng, or /dev/hwrng feed into haveged or rngd) so the kernel pool seeds quickly. On modern kernels the value is fixed at 256 once seeded and is not actionable beyond ensuring the initial seed succeeds.

checks.label: Widevine DRM Security Level
checks.description: Widevine DRM security level: L1 = hardware-backed (TEE), L2 = TEE for crypto only, L3 = software-only. Payment and streaming apps relying on Widevine assume L1; L3 indicates weakened hardware trust (often after root or custom ROM). Informational; the report shows the captured level for triage.
checks.remediation: L3 on a device that ships with L1 hardware suggests the TEE attestation is broken, the bootloader is unlocked, or the device is custom-ROM'd. Investigate the cause; reflash stock firmware if integrity is required.

checks.label: Metadata Encryption and Cryptographic Erase Support
checks.command: S=$(getprop ro.build.version.sdk 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$S" ]; then echo NOT_ANDROID; else M=$(getprop ro.crypto.metadata.enabled 2>/dev/null); T=$(getprop ro.crypto.type 2>/dev/null); V=$(ls -d /metadata/vold/metadata_encryption 2>/dev/null); echo "metadata_enabled=${M:-unset} crypto_type=${T:-unset} keydir=${V:+present}${V:-absent}"; fi
checks.description: Reports whether metadata encryption is in use alongside file-based encryption. FBE leaves filesystem metadata, including directory structure and file sizes, unencrypted unless metadata encryption is also enabled, and the metadata encryption key is what a factory reset destroys to make the userdata partition cryptographically unrecoverable. Without it a factory reset does not reliably render extracted flash unreadable, which is the guarantee an enterprise or payment deployment depends on when devices are decommissioned or resold. Passes when metadata encryption is enabled or when file-based encryption is at least confirmed active. Reports NOT_ANDROID and passes on a non-Android target reached over SSH or UART, where the ro.crypto properties do not exist and failing on their absence would be a false positive.
checks.remediation: Enable metadata encryption in the device fstab with the keydirectory option on /metadata, and confirm a factory reset destroys the key rather than only deleting files.
checks.why: Without metadata encryption a factory reset does not cryptographically erase userdata, so extracted flash may remain recoverable.
checks.risk_if_fail: A decommissioned or stolen device can yield recoverable data from raw flash despite a factory reset.
